root_cause_criterion.missing_conjunct: The pointer passed to `push_stack()` must not be the live stack-slot pointer `st->objs + n`; `copy_stack()` must copy `st->objs[n]` into temporary storage before the call.
root_cause_criterion.criterion: At the `copy_stack()` site that duplicates a live stack element through `push_stack()`, the actual argument must already be lifetime-decoupled from `st->objs + n` before the growth-path call proceeds, so `push_stack()` cannot `realloc(st->objs, ...)` out from under its own source object.
root_cause_criterion.description: In the vulnerable run, `push_argument` and `source_element_ptr` are the same tracked heap-slot pointer when the growth call executes and the protected `memcpy` sink later runs. In the fixed program, the same growth call and sink still execute, but `push_argument` is the address of the temporary copy while `source_element_ptr` remains `st->objs + n`.

nodes.state: `push_stack()` reaches `memcpy(temp, obj, sizeof(_cups_ps_obj_t))` with the tracked `obj` pointer still selected as the source operand at the AddressSanitizer-reported read sink.

`push_stack()` reaches the growth-path `realloc(st->objs, ...)` while its tracked `obj` argument from `copy_stack()` is still live, so the call invalidates that old stack-backed source pointer before later use.

edges.relation: The pointer `copy_stack()` chooses as the tracked `push_stack()` argument reaches the `push_stack()` parameter `obj` unchanged when execution enters the growth-path `realloc()` block.
After the growth-path `realloc()` has invalidated the tracked old stack-backed source pointer, `push_stack()` carries that same `obj` argument forward to the subsequent `memcpy()` read.
